}}'''Ruth Marion Lynden-Bell''', [[Royal Society|FRS]]<ref name="frs"/> (7 December 1937–27 April 2026) was a British chemist, emeritus professor of [[Queen's University Belfast]] and the [[University of Cambridge]], and acting President of [[Murray Edwards College, Cambridge]] from 2011 to 2013.<ref name="whoswho"/>

==Education==
Ruth Lynden-Bell began her education at [[King Edward VI High School for Girls]], Birmingham. She subsequently studied at [[Newnham College, Cambridge]] (BA 1959, PhD 1962) and studied under [[Norman Sheppard]]. She briefly studied under the direction of [[Harden M. McConnell]] at [[California Institute of Technology]] in 1961.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/page/women-chemistry-ruth-lynden-bell|title=Women in Chemistry, Ruth Lynden-Bell {{!}} Department of Chemistry|website=www.ch.cam.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=2018-08-07}}</ref> Then she became a lecturer in chemistry at the [[University of Sussex]] in 1965, and returned to Cambridge in 1972.<ref name="Lynden-Bell">{{cite journal |last1=Lynden-Bell |first1=Ruth M. |title=My Life in Changing Times: New Ideas and New Techniques |journal=Annual Review of Physical Chemistry |date=20 April 2021 |volume=72 |issue=1 |pages=35–50 |doi=10.1146/annurev-physchem-090319-054423 |pmid=33503383 |s2cid=231758540 |issn=0066-426X|doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Research and academic career==
Lynden-Bell's research used [[Molecular modelling|atomistic simulation]] to investigate the properties of liquids.<ref name="googlescholar">{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.co.uk/scholar?q=ruth+lynden+bell|title = Google Scholar}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Del Pópolo | first1 = M. G. | last2 = Lynden-Bell | first2 = R. M. | authorlink2 = Ruth Lynden-Bell| last3 = Kohanoff | first3 = J. | doi = 10.1021/jp044414g | title = Ab Initio Molecular Dynamics Simulation of a Room Temperature Ionic Liquid | journal = The Journal of Physical Chemistry B | volume = 109 | issue = 12 | pages = 5895–5902 | year = 2005 | pmid =  16851642}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Lynden-Bell | first1 = R. M. | authorlink1 = Ruth Lynden-Bell| last2 = Del Pópolo | first2 = M. G. | last3 = Youngs | first3 = T. G. A. | last4 = Kohanoff | first4 = J. | last5 = Hanke | first5 = C. G. | last6 = Harper | first6 = J. B. | last7 = Pinilla | first7 = C. C. | doi = 10.1021/ar700065s | title = Simulations of Ionic Liquids, Solutions, and Surfaces | journal = Accounts of Chemical Research | volume = 40 | issue = 11 | pages = 1138–1145 | year = 2007 | pmid =  17914887| s2cid = 2958411 | url = https://pure.qub.ac.uk/ws/files/500048/ar700065s.pdf }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Pinilla | first1 = C. | last2 = Del Pópolo | first2 = M. G. | last3 = Lynden-Bell | first3 = R. M. | authorlink3 = Ruth Lynden-Bell| last4 = Kohanoff | first4 = J. | title = Structure and Dynamics of a Confined Ionic Liquid. Topics of Relevance to Dye-Sensitized Solar Cells | doi = 10.1021/jp052999o | journal = The Journal of Physical Chemistry B | volume = 109 | issue = 38 | pages = 17922–17927 | year = 2005 | pmid =  16853300}}</ref> In 1995, she moved to Queen's University Belfast as a co-founder of the interdisciplinary Atomistic Simulation Group (now the Atomistic Simulation Centre).

She was an Emerita Fellow of [[New Hall, Cambridge]] (now [[Murray Edwards College, Cambridge]]), and was an Associate of [[Newnham College, Cambridge]]. She was acting President of [[Murray Edwards College]] from January to December 2012. Lynden-Bell also served on the editorial boards of the [[Journal of Chemical Physics]], [[Chemical Physics Letters]] and Science and was an editor of ''[[Molecular Physics (journal)|Molecular Physics]]'' from 1998 to 2003, as well as having been a member of Boards of Electors to Professorial positions in Sweden, the Republic of Ireland, and Oxford and Cambridge Universities. She was a Professor in the School of Mathematics and Physics at Queen's.<ref>[http://www.qub.ac.uk/home/Graduation/HonoraryGraduates/RuthLyndenBell/ Honorary Degree information from] [[Queen's University Belfast]]</ref>

== Personal life and death ==
She was the daughter of David and Priscilla Truscott. Priscilla was the sister of [[Francis Skinner]]. Lynden-Bell married the astronomer [[Donald Lynden-Bell]] in 1961, then a researcher at Caltech; she joined him in California, then moved with him to Cambridge in 1962, to Sussex in 1964, and back to Cambridge in 1972.  They had one son and one daughter.<ref name="whoswho"/>

Ruth Lynden-Bell had her first child while at [[University of Sussex]] lecturing in a half-time position. She found that being an experimental spectroscopic chemist was highly conducive to her expectations as a mother. Her advice to women in the field is: 1.)" don’t be afraid to ask for things such as part time work. Apart from the Belfast job, every job I got was by asking for it", and 2.) "when opportunities arise take them, it’s worth trying. I never imagined going to Belfast".<ref name=":0" />

Lynden-Bell's professional and personal life is featured in the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]'s book ''Parent Carer Scientist.''<ref name=":0" />

She died in late April 2026, at the age of 88.<ref name="x983">{{cite web | title=In Memoriam: Professor Ruth Lynden-Bell (1937–2026) | website=Yusuf Hamied Department of Chemistry | date=2026-05-01 | url=https://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/news/memoriam-professor-ruth-lynden-bell-1937-2026 | access-date=2026-05-12}}</ref><ref name="j694">{{cite web | title=Professor Ruth Lynden-Bell FRS, 1937-2026 | website=Murray Edwards College | date=2026-04-30 | url=https://www.murrayedwards.cam.ac.uk/college-news/professor-ruth-lynden-bell-frs-1937-2026 | access-date=2026-05-12}}</ref>

* 2006 – elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]]<ref name="frs"/><ref name="frselect">(19 May 2006). [http://www-theor.ch.cam.ac.uk/news.html Royal Society Elections], ''[[University of Cambridge]]'', Department of Chemistry, Theoretical Chemistry News Page. Retrieved 2 December 2010</ref>
* 2009 – honorary doctorate from [[Queen's University Belfast]]<ref name="honor">Torney, Kathryn (6 July 2009). [http://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/news/education/graduations/queens-university-of-belfast-graduations-july-6-2009-14386041.html  Queen's University of Belfast Graduations], ''[[The Belfast Telegraph]]''. Retrieved 2 December 2010 ("Queen's University professor Emerita Ruth Lynden-Bell will be awarded Doctorates of Science for distinction in chemistry at a ceremony tonight.")</ref>
